stimulus:
Fragments to collide with whatever comes next. Treat each as a mechanism, not a metaphor:

- lichen: two organisms negotiating a single body; the border is the product
- tidal pool at 3 a.m.; salinity climbs as the water leaves, and only the stubborn stay
- a bell-founder tuning metal by shaving the inside, never the outside
- mycelial relay: the message is sugar, and the delay is the computation
- kintsugi: the fracture is made the load-bearing feature
- a customs form for ghosts
- sourdough starter inherited across 140 years; the community is the instrument
- a moiré pattern: two regular grids, one irregular emergent third
- the stonemason's rule: cut the keystone last, and only once the scaffolding is already doomed
- bird murmuration: every agent tracks seven neighbors and none tracks the flock
- an auction where the loser pays
- a lighthouse whose beam is the absence of a shadow
- rust as slow fire; glaciers as slow rivers; ask what else is a slow version of something fast
- the apprentice who is forbidden to measure and may only compare
- a map drawn at scale 1:1 and then folded

Now: invert one assumption nobody states aloud. Borrow one fragment's mechanism by force, even if it seems absurd. Prefer ideas that would make an expert say "that's strange, but I could test it."

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Shave the inside: degron-titrated AP-1 removal after the stimulus ends
ideas.description: Instead of perturbing the inducing signal (the 'outside'), use an acute degron (dTAG/AID) on FOS/JUN family members at graded times after a transient stimulus (e.g., wound, cytokine, or stress) and ask whether chromatin accessibility and the enhanced re-response persist without AP-1. If AP-1 is truly a memory mechanism, there should be a window where it is needed to write the memory but dispensable to maintain it, or the reverse; the shape of that window distinguishes memory writer from maintainer.

ideas.title: Kintsugi test: AP-1 motif edits at sites made accessible by prior stimulation
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or saturating mutagenesis at enhancers that gain accessibility after a first stimulus (ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN) to ablate single AP-1 motifs, then re-stimulate after rest and measure transcription (PRO-seq/reporter). Sites where a motif break abolishes faster/stronger secondary induction while leaving the naive first response intact identify the 'fracture' that is load-bearing for memory, not for response.

ideas.title: Auction where the loser pays: competition between AP-1 dimers and pioneer/other factors at memory loci
ideas.description: Titrate the levels of different AP-1 dimer compositions (FOS/JUN/ATF, with dominant-negative A-FOS as a decoy) and measure occupancy competition with other factors (e.g., nucleosome, STAT, NF-κB) by single-molecule footprinting or Fiber-seq on the same DNA molecules. Memory should show up as sites where the 'loser' state (a factor-displaced or nucleosome-occluded state) leaves a lasting cost, i.e., a persistent footprint after AP-1 itself leaves.

ideas.title: Moiré readout: single-cell multiome lineage-tracked comparison of two stimulus histories
ideas.description: Subject clonal cells (barcoded) to two regular stimulus trains (e.g., pulses with different periods) and use paired scRNA/ATAC plus live AP-1 reporters (FOS-HaloTag/JUN) to see whether the emergent third pattern, a clone-specific response not predictable from either train alone, is inherited across divisions. Heritability of the interference pattern within clones versus between clones, with AP-1 occupancy as the mediator, tests whether memory is carried by AP-1 state rather than by lineage noise.

ideas.title: Mycelial-delay test: the lag is the computation, so measure slow AP-1 dynamics and nucleosome turnover
ideas.description: Perform time-resolved CUT&Tag for AP-1 factors, H3K27ac, and a nucleosome-turnover/histone-age label (e.g., SNAP-tag pulse-chase) across days after a transient stimulus, then fit models in which the delay between AP-1 loss and enhancer decay is the memory timescale. Then test causality by optogenetically or chemically prolonging AP-1 activity for a short window and checking whether the persistence time scales with it, which would show that the delay encodes the history.
